entries.title: Figure-Ground
entries.text:
Figure-Ground

Figure-ground composition separates the subject from the field so the person or object reads in under a second. Contrast of tone, color, or focus does the split, and if figure and ground share the same value the diagram fails even if the acting is good.

Create this Figure-Ground

Narrative function

First read is survival. A face against a matching wall disappears.

A dark coat against a dark street disappears. The audience should not have to hunt the subject unless hunting is the beat (camouflage, a sniper, a ghost).

It is the wrong tool to solve with a fake halo on every shot. Sometimes the story is that they do not separate: a clerk eaten by an office, a dancer eaten by a crowd.

Then you are composing fusion on purpose. Clean edges help.

Dirty edges and busy wallpaper fight figure-ground unless the figure has a stronger currency: backlight rim, color, or a pool of focus.

How it works

Park the subject against a simpler or opposite field. A rim or backlight traces the outline.

A shallow plane of focus melts the ground. A costume change (dark on light, light on dark, a single saturated piece) is cheaper than a new set.

Check a squint test: if the silhouette dies when you defocus your eyes, the split is weak. Prompt: Clear figure-ground separation of [Subject] from background, contrast of tone, color, or focus so the person reads instantly.

When to use it

Use it as default whenever a person must be found immediately: coverage, posters, any beat that is not hide-and-seek. Do not separate a character who is meant to be eaten by the room.

Compared with similar shots

Silhouette is a hard version: figure as outline against a brighter field, interior detail sacrificed. Shallow Focus buys separation with optics.

Figure-ground can also be a sharp, deep picture with tonal contrast. Tonal Contrast is the graphic extreme of lightest versus darkest mass.

Cameo Lighting isolates with a pool against dark. Architexture may intentionally lose the person in the building.

SilhouetteIdentity is less important than shape.

Shallow FocusNothing else is invited.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Classical cinematography treats instant separation as manners: rim, backlight, and costume contrast so a face reads in a theater. Westerns park figures against sky.

Noir parks them against wet highlights. When a film withholds the split, it is usually a hide, not a mistake.

Prompt it

Name the split method. Clear figure-ground separation of [Subject] from background, contrast of tone, color, or focus so the person reads instantly.

Say dark figure on a pale wall, or sharp subject, background soft, or a rim outlining the coat. Do not write pops.

Use in Image Generator

Clear figure-ground separation of [Subject] from background, contrast of tone, color, or focus so the person reads instantly.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a matching suit on a matching wall. The tell is a hunt for the head.

The fix is a rim, a different backdrop value, a costume change, or Shallow Focus. If they should vanish, own it and stop claiming a portrait.

Questions

What is figure-ground in film?

It is the split between the subject and the field so the figure reads immediately. Tone, color, or focus can do the job. If the person and the wall share a value, the composition has not separated them.

Figure-Ground vs Silhouette

A silhouette is figure-ground taken to outline: the field is brighter, the interior of the body goes dark. Figure-ground also includes a fully lit face against a darker or softer field. Silhouette sacrifices face for shape. Figure-ground may keep the face.

When should I use figure-ground?

By default, whenever the audience must find the person in a glance. Withhold it when camouflage, crowd, or architecture should swallow them.

How do I prompt figure-ground for AI image or video?

State how they separate. Example: Clear figure-ground separation of [Subject] from background, contrast of tone, color, or focus so the person reads instantly. Add dark coat against snow, or shallow focus, or rim light. Models often blend subject and wallpaper.

entries.title: Tonal Contrast
entries.text:
Tonal Contrast

Tonal contrast, the contrast composition of lightest against darkest mass, organizes the frame as a fight of value with the subject as one of those poles. Graphic punch replaces mid-grey mush, so the diagram reads as a poster of value rather than a gentle range of detail.

Create this Tonal Contrast

Narrative function

Make a poster out of a frame and the eye cannot miss the subject. A white face in a black room, a black coat on a white street, a lighthouse beam cutting tar: value owns space more loudly than furniture.

It is the wrong tool for a scene that lives in complexion, food, or mixed daylight conversation. If you crush the mids, you lose the sweat.

Not every picture should be a woodcut. Tonal contrast is composition, not automatically Low-Key Lighting lighting.

You can shoot high contrast at noon with hard sun and deep shade. Low-key is a lighting ratio.

Contrast composition is where the masses sit.

How it works

Meter for the winner. Let the other mass fall off or blow, on purpose.

Hard light and a dark flag help. A backlight rim can keep a dark figure readable on dark.

Expose for highlights if the subject is the bright mass. Kill fill if the subject is the dark mass on a bright field.

Prompt: High tonal contrast composition with [Subject] as the lightest or darkest mass, graphic punch, no mid-gray mush.

When to use it

Use it for night hunts, moral binaries, graphic titles, and any beat that should read at a distance. Do not crush a scene whose information lives in the midtones.

Compared with similar shots

Low-Key Lighting is a lighting style with dominant shadow. Tonal contrast can also be a bright graphic (white wall, black figure).

Silhouette gives up interior detail. Contrast composition may still keep an eye.

Figure-Ground is the broader first-read split, including color and focus. Chiaroscuro is the painterly modeling of form with light and dark, which may be less poster-flat.

Void deletes the field. Contrast still has two masses.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

SilhouetteIdentity is less important than shape.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Sin City language turns faces and streets into ink and paper. The Lighthouse grinds value until salt, beam, and body are almost woodcut.

Both make composition out of value first. Grammar, not a comic-panel kit to steal.

Prompt it

Declare which pole the subject occupies. High tonal contrast composition with [Subject] as the lightest or darkest mass, graphic punch, no mid-gray mush.

Say pale face in a black field, or black coat on white concrete. Forbid even grey fill.

Use in Image Generator

High tonal contrast composition with [Subject] as the lightest or darkest mass, graphic punch, no mid-gray mush.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is muddy mid-grey. The tell is a face, a wall, and a coat all sitting in the same value band.

The fix is to pick the lightest or darkest mass and send the rest away with flags, exposure, or costume.

Questions

What is tonal contrast in film?

It is a composition built from strong light and dark masses, with the subject as one of those poles. The picture reads as a graphic. Mid-grey detail is reduced so value, not clutter, owns the frame.

Tonal Contrast vs Low-Key Lighting

Low-key is a lighting ratio: little fill, dominant shadow. Tonal contrast is where light and dark sit as shapes. A noon street with hard sun and deep shade can be high contrast without being a night interior. A low-key room can still be a soft, detailed face.

When should I use tonal contrast?

Use it when the shot should read as a poster: night, moral split, graphic title, a figure as a cut-out. Do not crush scenes that need skin, food, or mixed conversation detail.

How do I prompt tonal contrast for AI image or video?

Name the poles. Example: High tonal contrast composition with [Subject] as the lightest or darkest mass, graphic punch, no mid-gray mush. Say which one they are. Ban even illumination.

entries.title: One-Point Perspective
entries.text:
One-Point Perspective

Central vanishing pointAxial composition

One-point perspective in one point perspective cinematography squares the camera to a plane so receding parallels meet at a single vanishing point, often on the central axis. The result is tunnel depth or ceremonial order: a corridor, a nave, a hotel hall aimed at infinity or at a person.

Volume

Create this One-Point Perspective

Narrative function

Destiny has a vanishing point when the architecture agrees. Walk toward it and the world funnels.

Stand in the middle and the world presents. A small step off axis becomes a scandal because the construction was so true.

It is the wrong tool in a room with no parallel receding edges, or when the scene should feel found rather than designed. Forcing a tunnel onto a forest is a lie unless the trees were planted as a nave.

Centering a face is not enough. If the walls do not recede to one point, you have central framing in a box.

How it works

Align the lens with the centerline of the architecture. Keep verticals vertical (shift, a level, or a longer lens farther back).

Place the vanishing point on a face, on a door, or on empty infinity. A moderate wide (24mm to 35mm) shows the funnel.

Too wide bows the walls. Prompt: One-point perspective corridor toward [Subject] or through them, vanishing point on axis, Kubrick infinity.

When to use it

Use it for hotels, spaceships, naves, bunkers, and any fate that should feel designed. Do not square up a messy street and call it one-point because a face is in the middle.

Compared with similar shots

Leading Lines may converge without a full axial construction. Centered Composition plants the subject on the axis but may be a flat altar with no tunnel.

Vanishing Point is the meeting place itself and can sit off-axis in two-point perspective. Symmetry often arrives with one-point, but a tunnel can hide an unmatched object as the break.

Architexture may flatten facade as texture instead of aiming it.

Leading LinesArchitecture should point.

Centered CompositionControl, ritual, comedy, or fate.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

The Shining aims Overlook corridors at a point that feels like destiny. 2001: A Space Odyssey uses axial interiors as designed future.

Leon and The Grand Budapest Hotel also square halls and lobbies so order is the air you breathe. Grammar of construction, not a carpet to copy.

The Shining 1980The Overlook’s corridors and architectural interiors.

The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014Frontal hotel interiors and concierge compositions.

Prompt it

Demand a single vanishing point and a square camera. One-point perspective corridor toward [Subject] or through them, vanishing point on axis, Kubrick infinity.

Name the receding architecture. Say camera on the centerline, verticals true.

If the person is the target, put the point on them. If they are a gate, put the point beyond.

Use in Video Generator

A lone night porter stands centered at the end of a perfectly symmetrical hotel corridor. Locked axial camera, central vanishing point, balanced lamps and doorways. Hold still as one door on the far left opens slightly, breaking the order. No camera move.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a centered portrait in a hall shot from a corner. The tell is two vanishing points, a wall receding on one side only.

The fix is to move onto the axis until left and right converge together, or to own Vanishing Point as a two-point street.

Questions

What is one-point perspective in film?

The camera is square to a plane. Parallel receding lines meet at one vanishing point, often on the central axis. Halls, naves, and designed interiors become tunnels or ceremonies.

One-Point Perspective vs Centered Composition

Centered composition puts the subject on the axis. One-point perspective constructs space toward a single vanishing point. You can center a face against a flat wall with no tunnel. You can also shoot a one-point hall with the actor off to the side as a break.

When should I use one-point perspective?

Use it when architecture can funnel: hotels, ships, churches, bunkers, a fate that feels designed. Do not fake it in irregular space, and do not confuse a centered head with a vanishing construction.

How do I prompt one-point perspective for AI image or video?

Ask for one vanishing point on axis and a square camera. Example: One-point perspective corridor toward [Subject] or through them, vanishing point on axis, Kubrick infinity. Name the corridor. Add verticals true.

entries.title: Vanishing Point
entries.text:
Vanishing Point

A vanishing point in vanishing point composition is the apparent meeting place of parallel lines in perspective, a destination for rails, a road, or a colonnade. The person often stands as a gate in front of that meeting, or occupies it as the target of the architecture.

Create this Vanishing Point

Narrative function

There is a long way still to go when the point sits beyond the figure. Space owns the future.

The body is a threshold, not the altar. If the point sits on the face, the architecture aims at them like a weapon or a blessing.

It is the wrong tool in a flat elevation with no receding parallels. A painted backdrop that does not converge cannot offer a vanishing point.

You would be naming a ghost. One-point, two-point, and three-point perspective all have vanishing points.

The compositional choice is where you put them, and whether the subject blocks, occupies, or is ignored by that meeting.

How it works

Stand where real parallels recede: tracks, a highway, a colonnade. Choose height (eye-level keeps the point near the horizon; a low camera lifts it).

Place the subject on the point, in front of it, or off it. A wider lens makes the suck toward infinity more violent.

Prompt: Deep vanishing point beyond [Subject], rails or road sucking the eye to infinity, the person as a gate.

When to use it

Use it when distance is the meaning: a road, a station, a landing site, a life still unwalked. Do not claim a vanishing point in a flat, shallow room.

Compared with similar shots

One-Point Perspective is the special case of a single, often axial, vanishing point with the camera squared. Vanishing-point composition can be a two-point street corner with the meeting off to the side.

Leading Lines steer the eye but may never meet in frame. Extreme Long Shot often includes a distant point.

The point is a location in the diagram, not a shot size.

One-Point PerspectiveDestiny has a vanishing point.

Leading LinesArchitecture should point.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Paris, Texas aims roads and rails at a horizon that keeps going after the man stops. Close Encounters builds landing-site perspective as a meeting with something that arrives from the point.

Stations, docks, and desert highways are the same grammar: infinity as a character.

Prompt it

Place the point and the person. Deep vanishing point beyond [Subject], rails or road sucking the eye to infinity, the person as a gate.

Name the parallels (rails, highway, colonnade). Say the point is on the horizon beyond them, or on their chest if they are the target.

Use in Image Generator

Deep vanishing point beyond [Subject], rails or road sucking the eye to infinity, the person as a gate.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a centered figure with no converging lines. The tell is a person in the middle of a flat field and a prompt that only says vanishing.

The fix is to include actual receding parallels, or to switch to Centered Composition and stop claiming perspective.

Questions

What is a vanishing point in film?

It is where parallel lines appear to meet in the picture. Roads, rails, and halls aim there. Compositionally it is a destination: beyond the figure, on the figure, or off to one side.

Vanishing Point vs One-Point Perspective

One-point perspective uses a single vanishing point and a camera squared to a plane, often on axis. A vanishing point also exists in two-point views of a building corner. One-point is a construction. The vanishing point is the meeting itself.

When should I use vanishing point?

Use it when distance should act: roads, tracks, naves, anything that still has a long way to go. Skip it in shallow, flat rooms with no receding edges.

How do I prompt vanishing point for AI image or video?

Name the parallels and where they meet. Example: Deep vanishing point beyond [Subject], rails or road sucking the eye to infinity, the person as a gate. If the point should sit on the body, say vanishing point on the chest, architecture aiming at them.

entries.title: Dirty Frame
entries.text:
Dirty Frame

A dirty frame in dirty frame cinematography lets out-of-focus shoulders, glass, foliage, or crowd chew the edges of the picture so the aperture is occupied. The camera sits inside a populated space, not on a seamless studio axis.

Volume

Create this Dirty Frame

Narrative function

Dirty versus clean edges is a moral diagram. Clean edges say the picture was granted.

Dirty edges say it was stolen, crowded, or survived. A shoulder in the foreground, a plant slicing a corner, rain on a window: someone else owns the near space.

It is the wrong tool for a product, a formal portrait, or a ritual altar. If the edges are dirty because the set was not cleared, you have clutter, not voyeur layers.

A dirty frame can still be composed. The chew should be intentional shapes, not a boom or a coffee cup.

How it works

Put matter close to the four edges or to the ones that should feel occupied. Open the aperture so that matter melts, unless a sharp shoulder is the eavesdropper.

A longer lens compresses crowd into the edges. A wider lens needs objects truly near the glass.

Check that faces still clear a hole in the middle. Prompt: Dirty frame around [Subject], out-of-focus shoulders, glass, foliage, or crowd chewing the edges, voyeur layers.

When to use it

Use it for surveillance, parties, streets, and any view that should feel unauthorized or crowded. Do not dirty a ceremonial single or a product hold.

Compared with similar shots

Foreground Interest is a salient near object that may sit in one region. Dirty frame is specifically about edges being occupied, often all around.

Frame within Frame cuts a hard inner rectangle. Dirty matter is usually soft and irregular.

Voyeur is the concealment position that often produces dirty edges. Clean Frame is the opposite ethic: empty edges, isolation by tidiness.

Layered Depth may keep those edge layers sharp if they carry action.

Foreground InterestPut air and obstacle between us and them.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

The Conversation watches through crowds, glass, and occupied space so privacy is already compromised. Children of Men keeps debris, bodies, and near matter in the aperture so the future never grants a poster.

Grammar of occupancy, not a blur sticker.

Prompt it

Occupy the edges and name the matter. Dirty frame around [Subject], out-of-focus shoulders, glass, foliage, or crowd chewing the edges, voyeur layers.

Say which edges (left shoulder, bottom foliage, rain-streaked glass). Keep a readable hole for the subject.

Forbid clean margins.

Use in Image Generator

Dirty frame around [Subject], out-of-focus shoulders, glass, foliage, or crowd chewing the edges, voyeur layers.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is accidental clutter, or a Clean Frame with a fake vignette. The tell is a boom, a logo, or a blurry oval that is not an object.

The fix is to choose the occluders, place them on the edges, and open the lens so they melt without covering the mouth.

Questions

What is a dirty frame in film?

Out-of-focus or near matter chews the edges: shoulders, glass, foliage, crowd. The view is occupied. The camera feels inside a space we were not invited to stand in, or inside a crowd that will not clear.

Dirty Frame vs Clean Frame

A dirty frame occupies the edges. A clean frame keeps them empty of accident. One isolates by obstruction and complicity. The other isolates by tidiness. Choose the ethic. Do not mix them by forgetting to clear a table.

When should I use a dirty frame?

Use it when the view should feel stolen, crowded, or physically situated: surveillance, parties, streets, affairs. Do not use it on a formal altar or a product.

How do I prompt dirty frame for AI image or video?

Name the occluders and the edges. Example: Dirty frame around [Subject], out-of-focus shoulders, glass, foliage, or crowd chewing the edges, voyeur layers. Models default to clean margins. You must demand occupied edges.

entries.title: Clean Frame
entries.text:
Clean Frame

A clean frame in clean frame cinematography keeps the edges empty of accidental objects so isolation arrives by tidiness, not by blur. The diagram has no landlord in the corners, which is studio-poster clarity even on a real street.

Create this Clean Frame

Narrative function

Nothing extra. Who owns space is whoever you left in the rectangle.

A driver against night, a bottle on seamless, a dancer in a cleared hall: the edges do not argue. It is the wrong tool for eavesdropping and for documentary crowding.

, a clean frame may be a lie unless someone in the story has already tidied for an inspection. Clean is not the same as empty.

A fully dressed set can still be clean if no lamp, plant, or shoulder nicks the four sides. Negative space is extra emptiness.

Clean is extra discipline.

How it works

Clear the near field. Watch all four edges on the monitor.

Use flags and art department, not only a long lens. A longer lens helps by excluding, but a wide clean frame is a stronger claim: you composed the whole room and still kept the borders empty.

Stop down if you need the empty walls sharp. Prompt: Clean frame of [Subject], edges empty, no accidental objects, studio-poster clarity, isolation by tidiness.

When to use it

Use it for product, ritual, poster portraits, and any character who lives in control. Do not clean a view that should feel stolen.

Compared with similar shots

Dirty Frame occupies the edges. That is the opposite ethic.

Negative Space makes emptiness a mass, which a clean frame may also do, but a clean frame can be full of designed set as long as the borders are tidy. Centered Composition often wants clean edges so the altar is not nibbled.

Void deletes the world. Clean still allows a world, just a disciplined one.

Negative SpaceLoneliness needs room.

Centered CompositionControl, ritual, comedy, or fate.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Drive isolates night figures and cars with poster discipline: edges held, little accident. Product cinema clears tables until an object is a monument.

The grammar is control. A scuff on that control should be intended.

Prompt it

Forbid the corners. Clean frame of [Subject], edges empty, no accidental objects, studio-poster clarity, isolation by tidiness.

Say no foreground occluders, margins clear. If the set is dressed, add fully dressed room, edges still empty of accident.

Use in Image Generator

Clean frame of [Subject], edges empty, no accidental objects, studio-poster clarity, isolation by tidiness.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a dirty street pretending to be a poster, or a Void you got by turning off the lights. The tell is a stray shoulder, a plant in the corner, or a black field with no place.

The fix is to clear the edges or to admit you wanted occupied edges and shoot Dirty Frame.

Questions

What is a clean frame in film?

The edges are empty of accidental objects. Every inch is chosen. Isolation comes from tidiness. The camera is granted a view, not a peephole.

Clean Frame vs Negative Space

Negative space is a large empty mass that acts in the story. A clean frame is about edges without accident. You can have a crowded, designed interior that is still clean at the borders. You can also have dirty edges around a tiny figure in a huge sky.

When should I use a clean frame?

Use it for control, product, ritual, and poster isolation. Do not tidy a stolen view or a documentary crush.

How do I prompt clean frame for AI image or video?

Ban occluders. Example: Clean frame of [Subject], edges empty, no accidental objects, studio-poster clarity, isolation by tidiness. Add no foreground objects at the edges. Models love plants in corners. Forbid them.

entries.title: Look Space
entries.text:
Look Space

Look-object relationshipRaccord regard

Look space framing is the field in front of a gaze, the air a look owns, often because the important object is off-screen. In cutting, that look may be joined to what is seen (raccord regard, the look-object relationship).

Create this Look Space

Narrative function

A face and a rectangle of unused air can be a whole scene. We wait for the object: a person entering, a painting, a courtyard window.

The subject does not own the surplus. The unseen does.

It is the wrong tool when there is no look. Empty space beside a face that stares into lens is not look-space.

It is leftover. If you need the object on-screen, put it there and stop pretending the air is a mystery.

Look-space is the composition. The POV cut is the completion.

You can hold the look and never pay off, which is a different cruelty.

How it works

Place more frame in the gaze direction than behind the head, unless you are short-siding. Match the height and direction of the look if the next shot is the object.

A profile or three-quarter makes the owned field obvious. Do not fill that field with competing faces unless the competition is the point.

Prompt: Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see.

When to use it

Use it when the object of attention is off-screen or about to enter: a watcher, a painter, a sniper, a lover at a door. Do not leave dead air beside a to-camera interview and call it a look.

Compared with similar shots

Lead Room includes motion and classical manners for a walk. Look-space is specifically the gaze, especially toward an off-screen object.

Point of View is the shot of what they see. Look-space is the shot of them seeing.

Short Siding withholds this field. Reaction Shot may be a look with almost no space if the face is the whole event.

Frame within Frame can put the object in a window inside the look-space.

Lead RoomThey are going somewhere, even if standing.

Point of ViewForce identification. The audience is the character.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Rear Window builds Jeff's looks and then pays them with courtyard activity. Portrait of a Lady on Fire makes looking the subject, space between painter and model as the true field.

The Stendhal Syndrome matches Anna's looks to museum paintings. Grammar of eyeline, not a tourist view to copy.

Rear Window 1954Jeff looks out, followed by views of courtyard activity.

The Stendhal Syndrome 1996Anna’s looks are matched to museum paintings.

Prompt it

Give the gaze a field and keep the object off unless you want it. Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see.

Say looking screen-left into empty frame, object not shown. If you will cut to Point of View, write that as a second shot.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: a seated woman looks upward and to her left toward a sound. Generate B: a slightly elevated wall clock seen from her seated side of the room. Generate C: return to her face as she understands she is late. Preserve look direction and plausible clock height.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is leftover wallpaper, or a false eyeline cut. The tell is empty space on the wrong side of the face, or a next shot the look could not geometrically reach.

The fix is to put the surplus in the gaze direction and to match height and angle if you complete the look.

Questions

What is look space in film?

It is the area of frame a gaze owns, usually ahead of the eyes. Often the important object is off-screen, so the air is tension. In editing, the look may be joined to a shot of what is seen.

Look Space vs Lead Room

Lead room is space in the direction of movement, and by extension a standing look. Look space is the gaze as a relationship to an object, present or withheld. A runner needs lead room. A watcher of a courtyard needs look-space. They overlap in a still profile. They are not the same job.

When should I use look space?

Use it when what matters is off-screen or about to arrive, and the face watching is the present tense. Do not confuse leftover margin on an interview with a look.

How do I prompt look space for AI image or video?

Point the eyes and empty the field they face. Example: Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see. Say the object is not in frame. For video, you can add a second shot as POV.

entries.title: Architexture
entries.text:
Architexture

Architexture, a nickname for architectural cinematography that treats the set as subject, fills the frame with facades, grids, and materials until a person is a detail of the building. Texture, module, and mass own space, and the body is an ornament or a scale figure.

Create this Architexture

Narrative function

When the set is the subject, human plot becomes a visitor. Concrete, glass, carpet, and window bands do the talking.

A figure gives scale, then disappears into the pattern. It is the wrong tool when a close-up of a lie is the scene.

Architecture cannot deliver an eye twitch. If you drown a dialogue in facade, you will photograph a building and call it a conversation.

This is not automatically one-point ceremony. A flat elevation, a brutalist soffit, a repeating office ceiling can be architexture without a vanishing tunnel.

How it works

Expose for the material: raking light for relief, or flat light for graphic grids. Use a longer lens to compress floors into texture, or a wide lens close to a wall so the body is tiny against a single plane.

Stop down so brick and joint stay sharp if texture is the point. Prompt: Architecture as texture around [Subject], facades, grids, and materials filling the frame until the person is a detail of the building.

When to use it

Use it when place outweighs person: first arrival in a city, a worker in a machine, a critic of a monument. Do not use it as the only coverage of an intimate scene.

Compared with similar shots

One-Point Perspective aims space as a tunnel. Architexture may be a flat, tactile wall.

Repetition and Pattern counts units. Architexture can be irregular material, poured and stained.

Extreme Long Shot shrinks a person in land. This shrinks them in built matter.

Windows makes apertures the subject. Architexture may have almost no people in those apertures.

One-Point PerspectiveDestiny has a vanishing point.

Repetition and PatternSystems, armies, hotels, factories.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Playtime (PlayTime) lets modern Paris eat its visitors: glass, grid, and waiting room as comedy of texture. The Brutalist language puts poured mass and material ahead of comfort.

The person remains, as scale. Grammar of buildings, not a tourist postcard.

Prompt it

Let the building win. Architecture as texture around [Subject], facades, grids, and materials filling the frame until the person is a detail of the building.

Name the material (concrete board-form, glass curtain, hotel carpet). Say the figure is small in the architecture.

Do not crop as a portrait.

Use in Image Generator

Architecture as texture around [Subject], façades, grids, and materials filling the frame until the person is a detail of the building.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a human portrait with a famous building behind. The tell is a large face and a postcard sliver of facade.

The fix is to step back or go longer until the body is a module among modules, or to admit you wanted a portrait and drop the claim.

Questions

What is architexture in film?

It is composition that treats architecture as the subject: facades, grids, and materials filling the frame. A person remains as a detail or a scale figure. The set owns space.

Architexture vs One-Point Perspective

One-point perspective is a tunnel of receding parallels, often ceremonial. Architexture is material and module, which might be a flat wall, a ceiling grid, or a poured mass with no vanishing showpiece. They can combine in a designed hall. They need not.

When should I use architexture?

Use it when the building is the story: arrival, labor, monument, a system of rooms. Do not use it as the only shot of a face that must be read.

How do I prompt architexture for AI image or video?

Make the person small in material. Example: Architecture as texture around [Subject], facades, grids, and materials filling the frame until the person is a detail of the building. Name concrete, glass, or grid. Forbid portrait crop.

entries.title: Reflections
entries.text:
Reflections

Mirror dialogueOne-way-glass staging

Reflections in reflection cinematography put observer and observed in one plane by using glass, water, chrome, or a mirror. Mirror dialogue and one-way-glass staging let two spaces occupy a single composition, because optics, not a filter, do the doubling.

Create this Reflections

Narrative function

Show looking and the looked-at together and you skip a cut. A man and a woman speak through a booth.

A face and a street stack in a shop window. Identity splits without a dissolve.

It is the wrong tool when the reflection is an unreadable smear, or when it cheats physics (a mirror that does not answer a head turn). If you cannot map the sightline, the audience will feel the fake even if they cannot name it.

Reflections can dirty a frame or frame-in-frame a second world. Decide which space is brighter.

The brighter side writes itself onto the darker glass.

How it works

Map optics before you light. Control which side is hotter: the reflection needs a brighter source to read on glass.

Hide the camera, or let it appear if that is the joke. Keep gaze and reflection geometrically honest.

Polarizers kill or manage bounce. Water needs an angle and a still or living surface.

Prompt: Reflections of [Subject] in glass, water, or chrome, observer and observed in one plane.

When to use it

Use it for split identity, conversations that cannot be face to face, cities on windows, a child seeing a parent in a cabinet. Do not add a random mirror because the set has one.

Compared with similar shots

Frame within Frame uses a hard inner rectangle. A reflection may be a smear, a stack, or a perfect copy.

Silhouette can appear in glass as outline. Screen in Screen is an electronic or projected picture, not a bounce.

Dirty Frame often uses glass as an edge chew. Here the glass is the sentence.

Windows may include reflections, but windows as a technique are stacked apertures of lives.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

SilhouetteIdentity is less important than shape.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

The Lady from Shanghai multiplies positions in a mirror maze until aiming becomes impossible. Paris, Texas stages Travis and Jane across a one-way-glass booth so seeing is not symmetrical.

In the Mood for Love catches bodies in glass and rain. Contact uses a cabinet mirror in a child's race down a hall: reflection as geography.

Paris, Texas 1984Travis and Jane speak across the one-way-glass booth.

The Lady from Shanghai 1947The mirror-maze climax multiplies possible positions.

Contact 1997Young Ellie races for the bathroom medicine cabinet after discovering her father collapsed.

Prompt it

Name the surface and both occupants. Reflections of [Subject] in glass, water, or chrome, observer and observed in one plane.

Say shop window, one-way glass, puddle, or chrome. State who is real in front of the surface and who appears in it.

Add camera hidden if the camera must not appear.

Use in Video Generator

A man and woman speak across a one-way-glass booth. Her illuminated face is visible while his dim reflection gradually overlays the glass as the light balance changes. Keep their positions consistent and the reflection optically plausible. Slow, restrained performance; no supernatural double.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a pasted-on double, or a mirror that ignores head movement. The tell is a reflection that does not match angle, brightness, or motion.

The fix is to build a real optic: brighter observed side, correct eyeline, and a surface that could actually see both.

Questions

What is reflections in film?

Glass, water, chrome, or a mirror puts two spaces into one picture. Observer and observed can share a plane. The bounce must obey optics: angle, brightness, and motion.

Reflections vs Frame within Frame

A frame within a frame is a second rectangle, often a door or window opening. A reflection is an optical copy or overlay on a surface. A window can do both: it can be an aperture and a mirror at once if you light both sides.

When should I use reflections?

Use them to show looking and the looked-at together, to split a self, or to have a conversation that cannot be face to face. Do not insert a mirror as furniture with no optical job.

How do I prompt reflections for AI image or video?

Name the surface and both parties. Example: Reflections of [Subject] in glass, water, or chrome, observer and observed in one plane. Specify one-way glass, shop window, or water. For video, demand the reflection match head movement.

entries.title: Screen in Screen
entries.text:
Screen in Screen

Desktop filmInterface as the camera

Screen in screen (desktop film, interface as the camera) nests a monitor, phone, television, or cinema inside the cinema so someone is watching a picture of someone. The inner image has its own crop, delay, and artifacts, and nested looking is the diagram.

Create this Screen in Screen

Narrative function

A picture of a picture changes ownership. The person on the inner screen is already framed by someone else: a director, a hacker, a parent, a god.

We watch the watcher, or we become them if the interface takes over the outer frame. It is the wrong tool when the inner screen is an unreadable glow.

If text, faces, or timing cannot be parsed, you have set dressing. Desktop films live or die on exact writing and cursor behavior.

This is not split screen. Split screen is a graphic of two presents.

Screen-in-screen is a nested world with a power relation.

How it works

Design a real timeline and a legible inner frame. Photograph or generate the inner picture as an asset, then place it in a monitor with correct perspective, refresh, and reflections.

Do not ask a generator to invent stable UI and accurate text in one pass if the words matter. Prompt: Screen-in-screen of [Subject], a monitor, phone, or cinema inside the cinema, nested looking.

When to use it

Use it when looking is already mediated: security, live TV, a search on a laptop, a projectionist, a god's control room. Do not add a TV that plays nothing relevant.

Compared with similar shots

Frame within Frame is usually architecture. Screen-in-screen is a display with its own image.

Split Screen tiles simultaneous presents without one being a device in the other. Windows stacks architectural panes of lives.

Voyeur may watch a screen, but voyeur is the concealment ethic. Reflections can stack a face on a dark monitor, a hybrid.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

Split ScreenTwo rooms, one moment.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

The Truman Show makes the world a production watched on screens. Videodrome infects the watcher through the tube.

Searching and Unfriended run investigation and terror through interfaces whose text and timing are the coverage. Sherlock Jr.

lets a projectionist enter the inner picture. Grammar of nested looking, not a wallpaper of monitors.

Searching 2018The investigation is presented through screens, calls and digital activity.

Unfriended 2014The action unfolds through a computer interface and group call.

Sherlock Jr. 1924The projectionist enters the world of the cinema screen.

The Stendhal Syndrome 1996Anna’s perception carries her into a painting.

Paprika 2006Images and screens become passages between dream spaces.

Prompt it

Specify the outer view and the inner picture. Screen-in-screen of [Subject], a monitor, phone, or cinema inside the cinema, nested looking.

Name the device, the content on it, and whether we see the watcher, only the UI, or both. If text matters, write the exact words.

Keep the inner image stable.

Use in Video Generator

Create a desktop-screen short: a woman starts writing an apology email, deletes it, receives an old photo and opens a video call she hesitates to answer. Generate the photo and call footage separately. Build the interface, readable text, cursor path and notification timing with code or compositing. No unreadable AI-generated UI text.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a blurry TV set, or a fake Split Screen. The tell is unreadable text, melting UI, or two images tiled with no device.

The fix is to treat the inner picture as a designed insert with real words and a physically plausible monitor.

Questions

What is screen in screen in film?

A display inside the shot carries its own picture: monitor, phone, cinema screen. Someone is watching a picture of someone. The inner crop, delay, and artifacts are part of the grammar.

Screen in Screen vs Split Screen

Split screen tiles two or more presents as a graphic. Screen-in-screen puts one picture inside a device in the other. Power and mediation differ. A control-room wall of monitors is nested looking. A graphic half-and-half of two callers is split screen unless those halves are phones in a room.

When should I use screen in screen?

Use it when looking is already a broadcast, a search, a tape, or a show: surveillance, desktop investigation, a film within the film. Do not add a glowing panel with no content.

How do I prompt screen in screen for AI image or video?

Name device and inner content. Example: Screen-in-screen of [Subject], a monitor, phone, or cinema inside the cinema, nested looking. For UI stories, render text deterministically. Do not generate the whole interface as unstable video if words must be exact.

entries.title: Tableau
entries.text:
Tableau

tableau vivantFrontal ensembleCinematic frieze

A tableau (tableau vivant, frontal ensemble, or frieze) is a staged composition whose meaning develops inside a relatively fixed frame. Arranged bodies and objects form a living picture, so duration replaces coverage while the camera stays locked or nearly locked.

Create this Tableau

Narrative function

Hold the arrangement and the audience reads at their own speed: who stands where, who fails to move, who sneaks a gesture. Stillness makes a tiny action loud.

Comedy, ceremony, and dread all use that delay. It is the wrong tool when the scene needs chase geography or a close-up of a lie.

If you cut the tableau to pieces immediately, you shot a master and threw it away. If the arrangement has no readable relationships, you shot decoration.

Tableau is not automatically centered, but it likes a designed field. Dirty edges can still apply if the living picture is glimpsed from a door.

How it works

Block silhouettes, spacing, and sightlines before adding motion. Rehearse separate timings inside the shared frame.

Use enough depth of field that the intended points stay readable. A locked tripod is the default.

A slow creep is a different sentence. Prompt: Tableau of [Subject], arranged bodies, a living painting, duration instead of coverage.

When to use it

Use it for ritual, comic ensembles, processions, and any beat that should be discovered rather than prescribed by cutting. Do not hold a well-dressed but empty arrangement.

Compared with similar shots

Static Locked-Off is the camera lock. Tableau is the staged picture that uses that lock.

Centered Composition is a common altar for it, not a requirement. Group Shot is a size.

Tableau is duration plus arrangement. Triangular Composition may be the geometry inside the hold.

Long Take may travel. A tableau usually stays and lets time do the move.

Centered CompositionControl, ritual, comedy, or fate.

Static Locked-OffTrust blocking and duration. Movement would be noise.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Barry Lyndon holds painterly courts until a glance is an event. Roy Andersson's films park ensembles in still rooms so a small failure is comic and awful.

PlayTime distributes gags across broad, held compositions. The Color of Pomegranates arranges people and objects as ritual friezes.

Grammar of duration, not a freeze.

PlayTime 1967Office and restaurant scenes distribute comedy across broad compositions.

The Color of Pomegranates 1969Frontal, ritualized arrangements of people and objects.

Prompt it

Ask for arrangement and a hold. Tableau of [Subject], arranged bodies, a living painting, duration instead of coverage.

Name positions (left standing, center seated, right in a doorway) and say camera locked off. For video, add little motion except a planned gesture, no coverage cuts.

Use in Video Generator

Locked wide frontal shot of five museum attendants preparing a display. Each performs a different small task; one repeatedly moves an object that another immediately returns. Clear spacing, readable full-body gestures, dry visual humor, no close-ups or camera motion.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Master Shot you plan to chop, or a pretty still with no relationships. The tell is a posed group that exists to be pretty, then a cut to close-ups that do all the work.

The fix is to give each body a job and to let the hold be the coverage.

Questions

What is tableau in film?

It is a staged picture whose meaning develops inside a relatively fixed frame. Bodies and objects are arranged. Duration does the work that cutting would otherwise do. A living painting, not a freeze frame.

Tableau vs Static Locked-Off

Static is a camera that does not move. Tableau is an arranged field that uses stillness, usually with a locked camera. You can lock off a messy documentary corner and have static without tableau. You can, rarely, drift across a tableau, but the default is a hold.

When should I use tableau?

Use it for ritual, ensemble comedy, processions, and any scene the audience should read as a whole. Do not use it as a pretty pause in a chase, and do not cut it to bits immediately.

How do I prompt tableau for AI image or video?

Describe the arrangement and the hold. Example: Tableau of [Subject], arranged bodies, a living painting, duration instead of coverage. List positions. For video, specify a locked camera and a long hold with one planned gesture.

entries.title: Void
entries.text:
Void

A void in void cinematography erases the set: darkness, white, or a blank field eating the world until a figure stands against nothing. Negative space still belongs to a place, while a void deletes place, leaving almost no landlord but the body or the darkness that might eat it.

Create this Void

Narrative function

Erase the set and the social world goes with it. A woman in a black room, a man in white nowhere, a beam with no walls: there is no furniture to own space, only the figure and the absence.

It is the wrong tool when geography matters. A void cannot show a door, a class, or a weather.

If you still need the kitchen, you wanted negative space or cameo light in a real room. Cameo lighting can create a void by refusing to fill.

The void is the compositional result: no readable world, not merely a moody key.

How it works

Kill the surround. Black velvet, an unlit stage, fogged white, a clipped sky.

Light only the figure, or let them fall to Silhouette on nothing. Watch for stray stand legs and floor bounce.

A longer lens helps exclude leftover set. Prompt: Void around [Subject], darkness or blank field eating the world, a figure against nothing.

When to use it

Use it for existential isolation, alien rooms, interrogation nowhere, a mind. Do not use it as a cheap way to hide a location you did not dress.

Compared with similar shots

Negative Space keeps a world (sky, wall, sea) as the empty mass. Void removes the world.

Cameo Lighting is the lighting method that often produces a dark void: a pool on a figure, no environment. Clean Frame still allows a tidy place.

Silhouette is outline against a brighter field, which can be a void if that field is featureless. Low-Key Lighting may still show a room in the shadows.

Negative SpaceLoneliness needs room.

Cameo LightingErase the world. Keep the person.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Under the Skin uses black, featureless space as a place that is not a place, bodies without social furniture. The Lighthouse isolates men in weather and dark until the world feels eaten, more void than village.

Grammar of deletion, not a crushed exposure accident.

Prompt it

Delete the place. Void around [Subject], darkness or blank field eating the world, a figure against nothing.

Say black void, no set, no floor detail, or white featureless field. Light only the figure.

Forbid furniture and windows.

Use in Image Generator

Void around [Subject], darkness or blank field eating the world, a figure against nothing.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an underexposed room, or Negative Space with a visible wall. The tell is a baseboard, a plant, or grainy wallpaper in the dark.

The fix is to actually kill the surround (velvet, distance, flags), or to own the wall as designed emptiness.

Questions

What is void in film?

It is a composition that erases the set. The figure stands against darkness, white, or a blank field. There is no readable place. Absence is not a sky or a wall. It is nothing.

Void vs Negative Space

Negative space is empty area inside a world: desert, ceiling, sea. Void deletes the world. A nun under a pale church wall is negative space. A body in featureless black is a void. Both isolate. Only one still has geography.

When should I use void?

Use it when place should vanish: alien interior, mind, interrogation nowhere, existential isolation. Do not use it to hide an undressed set that still needs to be a room.

How do I prompt void for AI image or video?

Forbid the set. Example: Void around [Subject], darkness or blank field eating the world, a figure against nothing. Add no environment, no furniture. Specify black or white. Models love to invent rooms. Ban them.

entries.title: Voyeur
entries.text:
Voyeur

Unseen sound sourceSound beyond the frame

Voyeur cinematography places the camera in concealment so the audience is trespassing: a view through foliage, glass, a grate, or a distant window, often with dirty edges. The diagram is a peephole, not coverage, and the owner of that hide does not want us there.

Volume

Create this Voyeur

Narrative function

The audience is trespassing. That is the beat.

A couple through blinds, a conversation across a square, a tent at night: we occupy a hiding place. The subject does not present.

They are caught, or they would be if they turned. It is the wrong tool for granted intimacy.

A close-up the character knows about is not voyeur. An over-the-shoulder in a dialogue scene is coverage, even if a shoulder dirties the edge.

Offscreen sound often rides with this view (a whistle, a courtyard, a tent wall) because the hide limits what we can see. The technique itself is the concealed camera, not the soundtrack.

How it works

Put a real occluder between lens and subject and stand where a watcher could stand. Keep enough aperture to melt the hide (leaves, fabric, a slit) while holding the distant face.

A longer lens is the usual cheat for distance. Do not center the peephole like a pretty wreath unless the hide is a designed iris.

Prompt: Voyeur frame of [Subject], watching from concealment, dirty edges, a view we should not have.

When to use it

Use it when watching is transgression: affairs, surveillance, a neighbor, a hunter. Do not slap dirty leaves on a scene the character is performing for us.

Compared with similar shots

Dirty Frame is the edge grammar voyeur often uses. Voyeur is the ethical position: concealment.

You can dirty a party from inside the crowd without hiding. Over-the-Shoulder Coverage is dialogue coverage with a known listener in the foreground.

Frame within Frame may be a window we are invited to look through. Windows stacks many lives.

Voyeur picks one hide. Point of View claims we are the character.

Voyeur often claims we are not supposed to be anyone.

Dirty FrameWe are not supposed to have this view.

Over-the-Shoulder CoverageDefault dialogue coverage with spatial glue.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Rear Window makes looking across a courtyard the plot. The Conversation records and watches until privacy is a myth.

Cache (Hidden) holds distant, unauthorized views until the camera itself is an aggressor. M and The Blair Witch Project let presence arrive from beyond the visible, often as sound around a limited hide.

Grammar of trespass, not a leaf kit.

M 1931The murderer’s whistling identifies a presence beyond what is visible.

The Blair Witch Project 1999Night sounds suggest activity outside the tent and camera view.

The Usual Suspects 1995The final details destabilize the story that has been narrated.

Fight Club 1999Later information changes the meaning of earlier interactions.

The Sixth Sense 1999The ending reorganizes the viewer’s understanding of earlier scenes.

Rear Window 1954Jeff’s physical position limits what can be known about the courtyard.

Alien 1979The creature and ship’s spaces are revealed selectively.

Jaws 1975The shark is often suggested through effects and reactions rather than fully shown.

Touch of Evil 1958The audience sees the bomb before the ordinary street activity.

Rope 1948The hidden body’s location is known while guests remain unaware.

Prompt it

Name the hide and the forbidden view. Voyeur frame of [Subject], watching from concealment, dirty edges, a view we should not have.

Say through blinds, from behind a car, through leaves, a long lens across a courtyard. Keep the subject unaware.

Occupy the edges with the hide.

Use in Video Generator

Locked shot inside a dim railway waiting room. An unseen suitcase rolls across the platform outside; its wheels move audibly from left to right, pause, then return. The lone passenger reacts without the camera revealing the source. Design spatially coherent audio separately, with no visible creature or arbitrary musical sting.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a pretty Dirty Frame the subject could see, or an Over-the-Shoulder Coverage from a scene partner. The tell is eye contact with lens, or a hide that is only a vignette.

The fix is a real occluder, a plausible hiding place, and a subject who does not present.

Questions

What is voyeur in film?

The camera watches from concealment. The audience is trespassing. Dirty edges, distance, and a peephole often result. The subject does not offer the view. We take it.

Voyeur vs Dirty Frame

A dirty frame occupies the edges with matter. Voyeur is why we are standing there: we are hidden. A crowded street can be dirty without being voyeur. A clean, distant locked-off shot of an apartment can be voyeur without much edge chew, as in an unauthorized surveillance hold.

When should I use voyeur?

Use it when looking is a transgression: neighbor, spy, hunter, affair. Do not use it as default decoration on a scene performed for the camera.

How do I prompt voyeur for AI image or video?

Name the concealment and the unaware subject. Example: Voyeur frame of [Subject], watching from concealment, dirty edges, a view we should not have. Specify blinds, foliage, a grate, a long lens. Forbid eye contact with camera.

entries.title: Windows
entries.text:
Windows

Windows cinematography treats panes as the true subject: stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames. The diagram is a grid of possible pictures, not one doorway around one face.

Create this Windows

Narrative function

A facade at night is a contact sheet of other people's rooms. A courtyard is a theater of windows.

Who owns space changes per rectangle: a cook, a sleeper, a fighter, an empty kitchen. The building is a montage that does not cut.

It is the wrong tool when you only need one inner frame around one encounter. That is a single frame-within-frame.

If the other panes do no work, you photographed a house. Windows can be looked through from inside (rain on glass, a face and a street) or looked at from outside (Rear Window grammar).

Decide which side of the glass we occupy, and whether reflections will stack a second world.

How it works

Find a true grid: a courtyard, a block of apartments, an office elevation. Use a longer lens to flatten panes into a sheet of rectangles, or a wider lens if we are inside one room looking at many across a court.

Expose so more than one interior reads, or so most go dark except the one that matters. Prompt: Windows as the true subject around [Subject], stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames.

When to use it

Use it when many lives share a building, or when a single life is one pane among others. Do not use it as a pretty rain window on a portrait that never acknowledges other rooms.

Compared with similar shots

Frame within Frame is usually one inner rectangle. Windows multiplies them.

Screen in Screen nests electronic pictures. These are architectural pictures.

Voyeur may watch one pane from concealment. Windows can also be a public elevation, a city showing itself.

Repetition and Pattern counts the grid. Here the content of each cell matters.

Reflections may write the street onto the same glass.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

Screen in ScreenSomeone is watching a picture of someone.

Rule of ThirdsDefault dynamic balance. Break it later on purpose.

In film

Rear Window turns a courtyard of windows into a set of simultaneous shorts. The Hours uses windows as thresholds between interior lives and the weather of a city.

A building becomes an editing machine you can hold. Grammar of panes, not a single pretty rain glass.

Prompt it

Make the panes the subject. Windows as the true subject around [Subject], stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames.

Say courtyard facade at night, multiple lit interiors, or a wall of office panes. Place the subject in one rectangle among others.

Name at least two other lives or empty rooms.

Use in Image Generator

Windows as the true subject around [Subject], stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a single rain-streaked portrait, or a Frame within Frame doorway. The tell is one face and one glass with no other cells.

The fix is to show a grid of apertures and to give at least one other pane a life, even if it is only a lamp and an empty chair.

Questions

What is windows in film?

Panes become the subject: stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames. The composition is a grid of possible shots. One person may occupy one cell. The other cells still work.

Windows vs Frame within Frame

Frame within a frame is typically one inner border around the action, a door or arch. Windows multiplies apertures until the building is a sheet of pictures. A single window around a couple is doorway grammar. A courtyard of ten lit rooms is windows.

When should I use windows?

Use it when many lives share glass: apartments, offices, a courtyard at night, a city block. Skip it when you only need one threshold around one encounter.

How do I prompt windows for AI image or video?

Ask for stacked panes and multiple lives. Example: Windows as the true subject around [Subject], stacked apertures, lives in rectangles, a building of frames. Specify a facade or courtyard and more than one lit interior. Place the subject in one cell.
